items.note: 木 looks like a tree with branches and roots.
あお can also describe green things like traffic lights and fresh leaves.
Animal names are often written in katakana: イカ.
上 points up from a baseline.
土 is a sprout pushing up out of the ground.
Minecraft's melons are Japanese スイカ (watermelon).
Minecraft's tameable wolves are おおかみ (wolf), not いぬ.
Also はな 鼻 = nose (same sound, different word).
火 looks like a campfire with sparks flying out.
Minecraft calls the boat ボート, a loanword. ふね is the everyday word.
人 is a person walking: two legs.
はち also means 8 (八). Context tells you which.
Before です it often shortens to なん: なん です か (What is it?).
Japanese avoids あなた with people you know - use their name instead.
山 is three mountain peaks.
弓 is the shape of a bent bow.
目 is an eye turned on its side.
Two words, one sound: 蜘蛛 (spider) and 雲 (cloud).
Also 髪 (hair) and 神 (god) - same sound.
月 also means month: いちがつ = January.
Also 城 (castle).
Literally 'garden bird': にわ (garden) + とり (bird).
本 is a tree (木) with a line marking its root - the origin of knowledge.
川 (river) is three flowing streams. 革/皮 (leather, skin) sound the same.
Also 帰る (to return home) - same sound.
金 also means money: おかね.
石 (stone) + 炭 (charcoal) = coal.
Also 飴 (candy), with a different pitch.
Polite version: おはようございます.
The final は is the old topic particle, so it's pronounced 'wa'.
Sounds final; friends say じゃあね or またね.
Polite: おやすみなさい.
Use it to get attention, apologise lightly, or even to say thanks for trouble taken.
Also 風邪 (a cold, illness).
The Japanese Minecraft name for the furnace.
むら (village) + ひと (person); the ひ softens to び.
Rice is so central that 'rice' also means 'meal'.
Polite: ありがとうございます.
accept: ありがとうございます

items.note: Said before eating - try it before your next steak!
Said after eating.
Offering something: どうぞ.
Requesting something: みず を おねがいします.
Also read し, but し sounds like 死 (death).
Bigger numbers combine: じゅうご = 15, にじゅう = 20.
作業 (work) + 台 (stand).
今日 is a special reading: 今 (now) + 日 (day).
Also a soft way to refuse: ちょっと... (that's a bit...)
いっしょ に = together (with).
Also used as a title: やまだ せんせい.
Country + じん = person from there.
Country + ご = language.
暑い for weather, 熱い for hot things.
For weather. Cold things are つめたい.
速い = fast, 早い = early.
Irregular: its other forms come from よい (よくない, よかった).
For things, not people.
Shout あぶない! when a creeper sneaks up.
Near the speaker.
Near the listener.
Far from both.
A native word (鶴嘴, 'crane's beak') usually written in katakana.
